answer: Each agent must post a refundable staking deposit before its attestations count, and any peer can challenge a batch by paying a small dispute fee; when a challenge sticks, the losing side's whole deposit funds the challenger and auditors. A sybil therefore has to lock real capital on every fake plume of activity, and each ripple of disputes burns that stake, so attack cost climbs toward the zenith of total deposits instead of staying near zero as it would with free votes.
